"""Negative on the start of a number written after a word or sign in running text.

Component p-82af68dd@100000/layers.15.mlp.down_proj:4928 is mostly near zero. Its
large values are negative, and they fall on the tokens that lead into a number:
the space before it, and the first digit when that digit is a small label number.
The strongest cases are a space after a label word ("Grade 1", "Table 3",
"Zone 3", "Windows Server 2008"), after a month ("March 11"), or after a
comparison or math sign ("p = 0.0", "x + 2"). Weaker negatives come after an
ordinary word or a . , - mark ("Ser. No 10", "2 to 4").

The program predicts from the two newest tokens only:
  - a space after a label word or month: -3
  - a space after a comparison or math sign: -2
  - a space after a capitalized word: -1.8; after a lowercase word or . , -: -0.8
  - a "1" right after a space: -1.0, a "2": -0.5
  - everything else: 0

It explains about 6% of the variance (eval: about 4.5% before the digit rule). Token
identity alone explains about 5% and a lookup on (token, previous token) about 10%,
so most of the variance lies in context a short rule cannot see.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

LABEL_WORDS = {
    "Table", "Figure", "Fig", "Chapter", "Section", "Grade", "Page", "Line",
    "Zone", "Ward", "Type", "No", "Nos", "Vol", "Step", "Phase", "Level",
    "Part", "Article", "Rule", "Version", "Round", "Stage", "Class", "Model",
    "Series", "Windows", "code", "claim", "year",
}
MONTHS = {
    "January", "February", "March", "April", "May", "June", "July", "August",
    "September", "October", "November", "December",
}
MATH_SIGNS = {"=", "==", "<", ">", "<=", ">=", "≤", "≥", "+", "−", "×", "±", "%"}
PUNCTUATION = {".", ",", "-"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    """Activation at the newest token, from the newest token and the one before it."""
    if len(prefix.token_strings) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return carry, 0.0
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    before = prefix.token_strings[-2]
    word = before.strip()
    if token == " ":
        if word in LABEL_WORDS or word in MONTHS:
            return carry, -3.0
        if word in MATH_SIGNS:
            return carry, -2.0
        if word[:1].isalpha():
            return carry, -1.8 if word[:1].isupper() else -0.8
        if word in PUNCTUATION:
            return carry, -0.8
        return carry, 0.0
    if before == " " and token == "1":
        return carry, -1.0
    if before == " " and token == "2":
        return carry, -0.5
    return carry, 0.0

"""Layer 15, MLP down_proj, component 4929: a diffuse feature with no simple reading.

What the component is: one rank-one piece of the MLP output matrix. Its activation is
(hidden state . V_c) * ||U_c||. About a fifth of its weight sits on MLP hidden unit 4929
itself; the rest is spread thinly over the other ~6000 hidden units. Its activation is
roughly symmetric around 0.03, with standard deviation 0.28. It almost never passes the
causal-importance threshold, so switching it off barely changes the model's output.

What this program does: it predicts the component's typical value, about 0.03, at every
token, except at the first token of a document (or of a packed row), where the component
is essentially 0. Nothing simple beats this. Tested on training rows, the current token's
identity, the previous token, whether the token already occurred earlier in its document,
the position in the document, and token classes (digits, punctuation, non-ASCII, space
prefix) each explain at most about 1 to 2 percent of its variance, and the position-0
rule is the only structure that is clearly real.

What a table would add: a per-token lookup (about 30k entries) explains a little more,
about 2 percent of the variance on held-out rows, at the cost of being unreadable.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN_VALUE = 0.03  # typical activation away from a document's first token
FIRST_TOKEN_VALUE = 0.0  # the first token of a document: the MLP hidden state is near constant


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    first = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[t] != prefix.document_ids[t - 1]
    return carry, (FIRST_TOKEN_VALUE if first else MEAN_VALUE)

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 4930: a diffuse, unexplained small signal.

What it does: predicts the component's typical value, a small negative number,
at every token, except at the first token of each document (the start of a row,
or a new document packed inside a row), where the component is essentially 0.

Why: this component almost never matters. Its causal importance is ~0 on every
token checked, and switching it off barely changes the model's output. Its
activation has no readable pattern: token identity, the previous token, the
token's character class, position in the document and document-level averages
explain essentially none of its variance. The only good linear fit uses the
whole residual stream, which is not a concept. So this program captures the
mean level and the document-start zeros, and makes no claim about what drives
the component.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

TYPICAL_VALUE = -0.056  # mean activation over ordinary tokens (about -0.055 on training rows)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    # The first token of a row, or of a document packed inside a row, reads no earlier
    # context and comes out at ~0.
    starts_document = prefix.position == 0 or (
        prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    )
    return carry, 0.0 if starts_document else TYPICAL_VALUE

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 4931: a near-dead, token-agnostic component.

What it does: its activation is a small, roughly symmetric value (std about 0.27, mean
about 0.014) that no simple feature of the text predicts. Looking at token identity,
previous token, position, document or norms of the residual stream explains almost none
of it (held-out variance explained at most about 2% even with a per-token lookup table).
It is effectively off: switching it off changes the model's output by about 1e-6 nats.

This program predicts the simplest honest thing: the component's average activation at
every token, except at each document's first token, where it predicts 0 (at a document's
first token the activation is about 0 on average, since there is no earlier text).
"""

READS = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = 0.014  # average activation over the eval rows
FIRST_TOKEN_ACTIVATION = 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: position within the current document of the previous token (None at a row start)
    new_document = carry is None or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    position = 0 if new_document else carry + 1
    if position == 0:
        return position, FIRST_TOKEN_ACTIVATION
    return position, MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Constant predictor for layers.15.mlp.down_proj component 4932.

The component reads layer 15's MLP hidden state through one input direction. Its
activation is mostly carried by MLP hidden unit 4932 of layer 15 (correlation 0.57
with the activation over sampled positions), but its value is signed, roughly
symmetric around zero (mean -0.06, sd 0.85), and large values come in both signs.
Measured on training text, it is not predictable from the current token alone, the
previous token alone, the bigram, the position in the document, or the document as
a whole (out-of-sample token-lookup R^2 is at most about 0.01). Common word classes
(" of", sub-word fragments, digits, other words) have means within about 0.1 of the
overall mean, with " of" having sd 2.0 and both signs. Nothing simple found explains
the variance, so the honest description is the component's own mean level.

The program predicts that constant at every position and uses no context.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = -0.062


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    return carry, MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 4933: a context-driven readout with no simple reading.

What the component is: a rank-one piece of layer 15's down projection. It reads the MLP
hidden vector and its input direction is dominated by two hidden units, 4933 (weight
0.35) and 5767 (weight 0.20), with small weights on many others. Its activation is
roughly 0.73 * (0.35 * h[4933] + 0.20 * h[5767] + ...), where h is the unit's
SiLU(gate) * up value.

What this program does: it predicts the component's average activation (about -0.0066)
at every position. Over training rows, the activation (std 0.37) is almost unrelated to
anything a program can read from the text:
- token identity: holdout R^2 about 0.003 (about 0.02 with a heavily shrunk per-token table);
- the previous one or two tokens: R^2 at or below 0;
- character class (digits, punctuation, words, spaces), script, and newline: R^2 about 0;
- position in the document, and whether the token already occurred in the document: R^2 about 0;
- the model's own confidence (next-token entropy, probability of the top token): correlation
  with the activation |r| < 0.01;
- even the whole document's mean activation explains only about 3% (an oracle).
So the readable description is that the component is not a token or position feature; the
program's best constant prediction captures essentially none of the variance.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = -0.0066


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    return carry, MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 4934 of p-82af68dd: a near-silent, diffuse feature.

What it is: a rank-one piece of the layer-15 MLP output. It reads one direction of the
MLP hidden state (spread over many hidden units, not one neuron) and writes along a
direction that, read through the tied embedding, roughly promotes media and publicity
words (media, publicity, popularity, advertisement, YouTube, 传媒, 媒体) and suppresses
code- and URL-like tokens.

What it does in the model: almost nothing. Its causal importance passes the 0.1
threshold on none of 10 million corpus tokens, and switching it off moves the next-token
distribution by about 1e-6 nats per position. Its activation is a small, context-driven
value (mean about 0.02, sd 0.27) with no pattern a short rule captures: token identity,
script, previous token, position and repetition each explain almost none of its variance.

This program predicts the typical value, except on the genitive "of" particles
的 (Chinese), の (Japanese) and 之 (classical Chinese), where the component averages
about +0.35. That rule is the one pattern in the data; it explains about 0.2% of the
variance. A lookup table of per-token means would explain a few percent more, but it
would be a list of arbitrary token ids, so it is left out.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

TYPICAL = 0.02  # the component's mean activation over all positions
GENITIVE_PARTICLES = frozenset("的の之")  # Chinese 的, Japanese の, classical 之: "of"
GENITIVE = 0.35  # its mean activation on those particles


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    """Predict the component's activation at the newest token; it keeps no state."""
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    return carry, GENITIVE if token in GENITIVE_PARTICLES else TYPICAL

"""Layer 15 MLP down-projection, component 4936: a "subject-field noun" detector.

What it does, in plain terms: the component is switched on by content nouns that name a
field of human activity (science, industry, sport, business, games, software, a system or
process), more strongly when the same token has already appeared earlier in the document
and when the noun follows a determiner or preposition ("the industry", "of research").
It is pushed negative by nouns for abstract relations, quantities, places, feelings and
communication, and it is somewhat positive on Chinese (Han-script) tokens, which often
name such fields too. Everything else sits near zero.

How the program reads the text: it rebuilds the current word from its subword pieces (a
word starts at a token with a leading space or a non-letter), asks WordNet whether that
word is a noun and which kinds of noun it is, and checks the token's earlier occurrences
and the token before it in the same document. Weights were fitted by least squares on
training rows, in the activation's own units.

What it leaves out: the activation depends on context in ways this does not capture. A
per-token lookup table explains more variance (about 0.08 held out) but is a table of
token ids rather than a concept.
"""

import regex
import wordnet

READS = ()

# WordNet hypernym kinds: a noun that is a kind of one of these names a field or activity.
FIELD_KINDS = (
    "industry", "science", "sport", "business", "game", "software", "system",
    "medicine", "activity", "process", "device", "occupation",
)
# WordNet hypernym kinds for nouns the component dislikes.
ABSTRACT_KINDS = ("quantity", "relation", "location", "communication", "feeling")
# Words that open a noun phrase: determiners, quantifiers and prepositions.
OPENERS = {
    "the", "a", "an", "this", "that", "these", "those", "its", "their", "our", "your",
    "his", "her", "each", "every", "some", "any", "all", "many", "various", "of", "for",
    "in", "on", "with", "to", "between", "during", "about", "including",
}

BIAS = 0.062
NOUN, NOUN_AFTER_OPENER, NOUN_REPEAT = 0.132, 0.326, 0.418
FIELD, FIELD_REPEAT = 0.210, 0.513
ABSTRACT = -0.301
HAN, HAN_REPEAT = 0.069, 0.746


def _is_noun(word):
    return word.isascii() and word.isalpha() and "noun" in wordnet.parts_of_speech(word)


def _is_kind(word, kinds):
    return any(wordnet.is_a(word, kind) for kind in kinds)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_ids[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    piece = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if carry is None or carry["doc"] != doc:
        carry = {"doc": doc, "word": "", "seen": set(), "before": ""}
    repeat = token in carry["seen"]
    after_opener = carry["before"] in OPENERS
    carry["seen"].add(token)
    carry["before"] = piece.strip().lower()
    # Rebuild the current word: a piece with a leading space (or a non-letter) starts one.
    if piece.startswith(" ") or not piece.strip().isalnum():
        carry["word"] = piece.strip().lower()
    else:
        carry["word"] += piece.strip().lower()
    word = carry["word"]
    value = BIAS
    if _is_noun(word):
        value += NOUN
        value += NOUN_REPEAT if repeat else 0.0
        value += NOUN_AFTER_OPENER if after_opener else 0.0
        if _is_kind(word, FIELD_KINDS):
            value += FIELD + (FIELD_REPEAT if repeat else 0.0)
        if _is_kind(word, ABSTRACT_KINDS):
            value += ABSTRACT
    if regex.search(r"\p{Script=Han}", piece):
        value += HAN + (HAN_REPEAT if repeat else 0.0)
    return carry, float(value)

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 4937: a "select group / exclusivity" detector.

What the component is: almost all of it is hidden unit 4937 of layer 15's MLP (about 70% of
its input direction). Its output direction, read through the unembedding, favours "only",
"exclusive", "privileged", "elite", "alone" when the activation is negative. So it goes
negative on words that single out a small, select group ("only", "rare", "exclusive",
"authorized", "elite", "members", "subscribers", "few", "special", and their translations),
and a little on the few tokens right after them ("only [authorized] personnel",
"mainly [within]"). Most of its variance is a diffuse, small, context-dependent signal that
no word rule captures.

What this program does: predicts a negative value on a restriction word, and a fading
negative value on the next three tokens of the same document, with no state beyond the
last three tokens. It is a word-level rule, not a model of the neuron, and it explains only
a small part of the variance.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Words that name an exclusive or select group outright.
STRONG = {"rare", "exclusive", "exclusively", "authorized", "elite", "vip", "trusted",
          "privileged", "exceptional", "select", "selected"}
# "Only" and words that limit who or what is meant, in English and a few other languages.
MILD = {"only", "few", "special", "limited", "restricted", "members", "member",
        "subscribers", "eligible", "available", "accessible", "unless", "mainly",
        "mostly", "solely", "sole", "specific", "friends", "fans", "individuals",
        "wealthy", "certain", "仅", "只有", "也只有", "限定", "专享", "会员", "精品",
        "高端", "试点", "少数", "特权", "独家", "内部", "专属", "唯有", "nur", "solo",
        "solamente", "sólo", "seulement", "uniquement", "только", "alleen",
        "uitsluitend", "esclusivamente", "réservé", "exclusivo", "exclusiva"}

# Activation per restriction word, by how many tokens back it sits (0 = this token).
WEIGHTS = (-0.6, -0.4, -0.24, -0.16)


def _is_restrictive(token: str) -> float:
    word = token.strip().lower()
    return 1.0 if word in STRONG or word in MILD else 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    tokens = prefix.token_strings
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    t = len(tokens) - 1
    value = 0.0
    for back, weight in enumerate(WEIGHTS):
        i = t - back
        if i < 0 or docs[i] != docs[t]:
            break
        value += weight * _is_restrictive(tokens[i])
    return carry, value

"""Kind-of detector: component 4938 of layers.15.mlp.down_proj (Qwen3-1.7B, layer 15 MLP).

What it does
  The component is strongly negative on a word for a kind, type, sort or category of
  thing ("kind", "types", "sort", "variety", "genre", "tipo", ...) and on the "of" (or
  Spanish "de") right after such a word. These are the phrases "this kind of",
  "a type of", "different types of", "tipo de". The most negative values come after a
  determiner or quantifier ("this", "different", "two", "all"). After "the" or "a" they
  are weaker, and the same words used as code identifiers ("type", "\\ttype") weaker still.
  Other words that open a category phrase ("such as", "like", "range of") get a small
  negative value. Everything else is 0. The component's output pushes the model toward
  the word "type" (its negative direction raises "type", "类型", "tipo" in the logits),
  which is what these positions need.

  Predicted values are in the component's own activation units. Its typical strength is
  the table below; the rules and values are read off the component's activations on
  training text, not fitted to the model.

Why this version
  It explains about a fifth of the variance. Most of what remains is small, broad
  fluctuation over all tokens, which no short rule captures. A per-token lookup table
  does about as well (about 0.17 held out); the rule adds the determiner and "of" effects.
"""

READS = ()

# Typical negative activation of each category noun.
CATEGORY = {
    "kind": 20, "kinds": 20, "type": 15, "types": 18, "tipo": 25, "tipos": 25, "typ": 10,
    "sort": 10, "sorts": 12, "variety": 8, "varieties": 8, "genre": 8, "style": 6,
    "category": 5, "categories": 6, "class": 3, "species": 4, "genus": 6, "form": 3,
    "forms": 3, "size": 4, "quality": 5, "nature": 4, "degree": 3, "shape": 4, "level": 3,
}
# Words that open a category phrase, with a small typical value.
OPENERS = {"such": 2, "like": 1, "range": 3}
# Words before a category noun that make it stronger; other words make it weaker.
DETERMINERS = {"this", "that", "these", "those", "the", "a", "an", "such", "what",
               "different", "two", "three", "several", "all", "some", "other", "various",
               "any", "many", "another", "certain", "same", "every", "each"}
OF_WORDS = {"of", "de"}


def _word(text):
    return text.strip().lower()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = _word(prefix.token_strings[-1])
    before = ""
    if len(prefix.token_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        before = _word(prefix.token_strings[-2])
    value = 0.0
    if word in CATEGORY:
        value = -CATEGORY[word] * (1.0 if before in DETERMINERS else 0.5)
    elif word in OF_WORDS and before in CATEGORY:
        value = -CATEGORY[before]
    elif word in OPENERS:
        value = -OPENERS[word]
    return carry, float(value)

"""Predict component p-82af68dd@100000/layers.15.mlp.down_proj:4939.

What the component is: one rank-one piece of layer 15's MLP down projection. It
reads the MLP hidden state through an input direction that puts about 43% of its
energy on hidden unit 4939 (weight 0.57), and the rest is spread thinly over many
units. Its activation is therefore mostly that one hidden unit's value, scaled.

What it does in the model: almost nothing. It is essentially never important
(causal importance above 0.1 at no tokens in a 10M-token corpus), and switching it
off barely changes the next-token distribution.

What the activation looks like: centred near zero (mean about -0.03, std about 0.34),
with rare spikes of several units in either direction. I searched for a simple
explanation and found none. Neither the current token's identity, its character
class (letter, digit, punctuation, space, CJK), the previous token, the position in
the document, nor whether the token already occurred earlier in the document
predicts it on held-out rows (variance explained at most about 0.02).

So this program predicts the average activation at every position. It is the
best constant in the squared-error sense, and it explains essentially none of the
variance.
"""

READS = ()

# Mean activation over sampled training rows (about -0.033).
MEAN_ACTIVATION = -0.033


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Return the constant mean activation for this position."""
    return carry, MEAN_ACTIVATION


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Constant predictor: nothing to run. Use `eval` on this file to score it.
    print("predicts", MEAN_ACTIVATION, "at every position")

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 4940: a "fixing / remedy" word detector.

What it does: when this component's activation is negative, its output direction
promotes words about remedying something (read through the unembedding it pushes up
repair, remedy, fix, corrective, emergency, 修复, 解决, 应急 ...). Its large negative
spikes come on words where a fix, repair or response is the expected next idea
("resolving", "repair", "fix", "remedy", "timely", "quickly", "emergency", "to" before
a fixing verb). Most of its activation is small and noisy, and no token or word-class
feature we tried explains that bulk.

So the program predicts the component's typical value (about -0.04) everywhere, and a
clear negative value (-0.4, its mean on these words) on tokens of the remedy /
fixing / helping family. It is a conceptual sketch: it explains the sign and the
word family of the spikes, and very little of the variance.
"""

import re

READS = ()

BASELINE = -0.04
"""The component's typical activation: its mean over ordinary tokens."""

REMEDY_WORD = re.compile(
    r"help|helps|helping|fix|fixes|fixing|fixed|"
    r"repair\w*|remed\w*|resolv\w*|address\w*|solv\w*|correct\w*|treat\w*|cure|"
    r"heal\w*|restor\w*|mend\w*|patch\w*|emergenc\w*|respon\w*|protect\w*|rescu\w*|"
    r"prevent\w*|eliminat\w*|handl\w*|intervent\w*|urgent\w*|timely|quick\w*|"
    r"act|action|actions|save|recover\w*|mitigat\w*|tackl\w*|overcom\w*"
)
"""Words for fixing, remedying, responding to or acting on a problem."""


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    if REMEDY_WORD.fullmatch(word):
        return carry, -0.4
    return carry, BASELINE

"""Negative activation while the text is about help, assistance or services done for someone.

Component p-82af68dd@100000/layers.15.mlp.down_proj:4941 adds a small signal to the
residual stream. Almost all of its variance is in rare large spikes, and they are
negative. The spikes sit inside phrases where someone does, supplies or verifies
something for someone else: "help with", "assist", "guide", "hire a team of
professionals", "write my essay ... for you", "a tutor", "a calculator", "a solver",
"translate", "on behalf of", "someone". Its output direction points at helper words
(help, assist, 帮, 协助, 专业, automatically), so the signal is negative where the
text is about such help.

The program keeps a short memory of how recently a helper word appeared. The memory
jumps to 1 on a helper word and halves each token. The prediction is -SCALE times
the memory, and the memory resets at each document boundary.

What this captures: the sign and the rough location of the negative events, and a
little of the variance. What it misses: most of the spikes, which are not tied to
any single word. Single-token lookups explain nothing (variance explained about 0),
and so do bags of words over a window. The best lexicon found here explains about
0.5% of the variance on held-out training rows.
"""

import re

READS = ()

# Words about help, assistance, guidance, services and doing things for someone.
HELPER = re.compile(
    r"help|assist|guide|tutor|hire|professional|service|execut|generat|verif|review|"
    r"someone|somebody|friend|thank|calculator|solver|translat|behalf|advice|"
    r"帮|幫|协助|協助|助|替|代理|翻译|翻譯|专业|專業|服务|服務|代写|代寫|"
    r"помог|giúp|ajud|ayud"
)
DECAY = 0.7  # share of the memory that survives each token
SCALE = 0.7  # predicted activation at a helper word


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    memory = carry if carry is not None else 0.0
    new_document = len(prefix.document_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if new_document:
        memory = 0.0
    hit = HELPER.search(prefix.token_strings[-1].lower()) is not None
    memory = max(memory * DECAY, 1.0 if hit else 0.0)
    return memory, -SCALE * memory

"""Explanation of layers.15.mlp.down_proj:4942 (a rank-one piece of layer 15's MLP output).

What it is: one direction of layer 15's MLP hidden layer, written back into the
residual stream. Its activation is dense and noise-like: mean about +0.03, standard
deviation about 0.29, with no token, character class, or repeat pattern that predicts it.
Its output direction projects weakly and diffusely onto the vocabulary, with no clear
promoted or suppressed set of tokens. Its CI is essentially zero, so switching it off
barely changes the model.

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 4961: a weak, diffuse signal.

What it does: predicts the component's activation from two shallow facts about the
current token, and nothing else.

  1. How far the token sits into its document. The activation is near zero or slightly
     negative in the first few tokens of a document (about -0.07 at tokens 2-4) and rises
     slowly with distance into the document (about +0.08 by 300-500 tokens). The prediction
     is a log curve in that distance, fit on training rows.
  2. Whether the token continues a word. A bare alphabetic piece that follows another
     alphabetic piece with no space between them (the middle or end of a word split into
     several tokens) runs a little higher on average.

explains nothing on held-out rows), by the model's own next-token surprisal or entropy, by
repetition of earlier text, or by word-class features. Its variance is spread over many
hidden neurons and changes over about ten tokens with no single readable trigger. The
terms above account for under 1% of its variance.

import math

READS = ()

INTERCEPT = -0.112
LOG_DISTANCE = 0.030  # per unit of log(1 + tokens into the document)
CONTINUATION = 0.049  # added for a word-internal piece


def _is_word_piece(text):
    return text.isalpha() and not text.startswith(" ")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (tokens into the current document, document label of the previous token)
    if carry is None or prefix.document_ids[-1] != carry[1]:
        distance = 0
    else:
        distance = carry[0] + 1
    label = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    word_piece = False
    if distance > 0:
        prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip()
        word_piece = _is_word_piece(prefix.token_strings[-1]) and prev.isalpha()
    value = INTERCEPT + LOG_DISTANCE * math.log1p(distance) + CONTINUATION * word_piece
    return (distance, label), value

LATER_VALUE = 0.03

It is strongly negative on a short, uncommon English-letter token that starts or is a piece
of a word the model has not finished (" D" in "Diritto", " F" in "Fijian", " g", " ga", " li"),
most negative for a capital letter after a space, and it is near zero on common whole words,
long words, punctuation and digits. It is strongly positive on the chat-format markers
(<|im_start|>, <think>, <tool_call>, <tool_response> and their closing forms).

Plain-terms rule: a token that is 1-3 ASCII letters long and not a common English word
(wordfreq zipf < 6) gets a negative value, scaled by how short it is (1 letter -4, 2 -2.5,
3 -1) and by case (a capital after a space -1.3x, a lowercase piece after a space -1x,
a capital with no space -0.8x, a lowercase piece with no space -0.5x). Chat markers get +4.5.
Everything else is 0. Only the current token is read; no state is carried.
"""

import wordfreq

READS = ()

CHAT_MARKERS = {
    "<|im_start|>",
    "<think>",
    "<tool_call>",
    "</tool_call>",
    "<tool_response>",
    "</tool_response>",
}

SIZE = {1: 4.0, 2: 2.5, 3: 1.0}  # shorter fragments are more negative
COMMON_ZIPF = 6.0  # wordfreq zipf at or above this is a common word: no effect


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if token in CHAT_MARKERS:
        return carry, 4.5

    if wordfreq.zipf_frequency(word.lower(), "en") >= COMMON_ZIPF:
        return carry, 0.0
    if spaced:

    else:
        case = 0.8 if capital else 0.5

rare words that the tokenizer split into several tokens.

The unit is negative on a piece that continues a rare word: "back|com|bing",
"sh|aker", "Herbal|ife", "Guide|book". It is near zero on word-initial tokens,
on pieces of common words ("walk|ing"), and on punctuation and digits. Its
positive values (for example "отр|им|ання") follow no simple rule and are not
predicted here.

Prediction for each token:
  -0.9  if it continues a word: no leading space, letters only, the token before
        it is also letters in the same document, and the word so far (from its
        first piece through this one) is rare (English Zipf frequency below 3.5,
        which includes all non-English words);
   0.0  otherwise.
"""

import re

import wordfreq

READS = ()
PIECE = re.compile(r"[^\W\d_]+")
RARE_ZIPF = 3.5
RARE_VALUE = -0.9


def is_piece(token):
    return bool(PIECE.fullmatch(token.strip()))


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    toks = prefix.token_strings
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    t = prefix.position
    cur = toks[t]
    if t == 0 or docs[t - 1] != docs[t] or cur.startswith(" ") or not is_piece(cur):
        return carry, 0.0
    if not is_piece(toks[t - 1]):
        return carry, 0.0
    # Walk back to the first piece of this word.
    j = t
    while j > 0 and docs[j - 1] == docs[t] and not toks[j].startswith(" ") and is_piece(toks[j - 1]):
        j -= 1
    word = "".join(toks[j : t + 1]).strip().lower()
    if wordfreq.zipf_frequency(word, "en") < RARE_ZIPF:
        return carry, RARE_VALUE
    return carry, 0.0

What the component is: its activation is (MLP hidden vector . V_c) * |U_c|. The V_c
direction is dominated by MLP unit 15.4968 (weight 0.33; the next largest is 0.08), with a
long tail of many other units. Its activation is a diffuse, noisy number: mean about -0.026,
std 0.27. It is almost never important to the output (causal importance ~0). No simple
token concept explains it: token identity explains about 1-2% of its variance, and coarse
character classes (digits, punctuation, spaces, CJK) about 0.2%.

What this program does (the little structure there is):
  - The first token of each document is ~0 (no earlier context in the document).
  - Other tokens sit near -0.01 on average when the token is new to its document, and near
    -0.04 when that token already appeared earlier in the same document. The repeat effect
    holds at fixed position.

variance (Pearson r 0.06), and it leaves the model's output almost unchanged, as switching
the component off does. A constant at its mean explains 0%. A linear read of the residual
stream explains about 20% on training rows, but that is a 2048-weight table with no concept
behind it, so it is not used here.
"""

READS = ()

DOC_START = 0.0
REPEAT = -0.04
NOVEL = -0.01


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_ids[-1]
    new_doc = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    seen = set() if carry is None or new_doc else carry

    elif token in seen:

    else:

"objection" detector.

The component is mostly near zero, but it goes strongly negative on contrast words that open
an objection to what was just said, in any language: "..., but that would require...",
"Wait, but...", "However, ...", "Hmm, ...", "但是", "しかし", "pero", "mais", "но", "aber".
The push fades over the next few tokens, so the program predicts the contrast word's typical
strength on the word itself, then that strength shrunk by a constant factor on each later
token, until the next contrast word or a new document. A small constant is the average level.

It explains only a little variance: most of the component's variance is a dense background
with no simple word or context trigger that we found.
"""

READS = ()

# typical activation on the contrast word itself (negative = objection)
OBJECTION = {
    "but": -1.4, "however": -1.0, "wait": -1.0, "hmm": -1.0,
    "但是": -0.85, "可是": -1.3, "但": -0.8, "然而": -0.6, "しかし": -1.2, "けど": -0.6,
    "aber": -0.6, "pero": -1.1, "mais": -1.0, "но": -1.0,
}
DECAY = 0.4  # the effect shrinks to about 40% per following token
BASELINE = 0.05  # the component's average level


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    new_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if carry is None or new_doc:
        carry = (0.0, 0)  # (strength of the last objection word, tokens since it)
    strength, since = carry
    if word in OBJECTION:
        strength, since = OBJECTION[word], 0
        return (strength, since), BASELINE + strength
    since += 1
    return (strength, since), BASELINE + strength * DECAY**since

(almost exactly) that hidden unit, and its activation is that unit's value times the size of
its output direction.

What it does, in plain terms: most of the unit's variance is a noisy, context-dependent signal
that no simple token rule captures (token identity explains under 1%). Its clearest responses
are negative:
  * the "(" that opens the parameter list of a function definition
    (`def f(`, `function f(`, `func f(`, `void f(`, `public void f(`): strongly negative, about -2;
  * the "(" that opens the arguments of an ordinary call (`print(`, `foo.bar(`): mildly negative, about -0.4;
  * the role word `user` right after a chat-template `<|im_start|>`: about -1.1.
Everything else is predicted as 0. The values are least-squares fits on training rows.
On eval this explains about 1.7% of the variance (Pearson r about 0.13); it is a partial
account, not a full one.

import re

READS = ()

DEFINITION_WORDS = re.compile(
    r"\b(def|function|func|fn|void|public|private|protected|static|int|double|float|String|async)\b"
)
ENDS_IN_NAME = re.compile(r"\w\s*$")

DEFINITION_PAREN = -2.0  # "(" opening a definition's parameter list
CALL_PAREN = -0.4  # "(" opening a call's arguments
ROLE_USER = -1.1  # "user" right after "<|im_start|>"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if token == "user" and len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 and prefix.token_strings[-2] == "<|im_start|>":
        return carry, ROLE_USER
    if not token.lstrip().startswith("("):
        return carry, 0.0
    before = prefix.text_prefixes[-2] if len(prefix.text_prefixes) > 1 else ""
    line = before.split("\n")[-1]
    if not ENDS_IN_NAME.search(line):
        return carry, 0.0
    if DEFINITION_WORDS.search(line):

    return carry, CALL_PAREN

What it does, in plain terms: this component reads the MLP hidden state and writes one
direction into the residual stream. Across ordinary text its activation is a dense,
context-dependent signal: it has no clear dependence on the token, the previous token, the
position, or the simple character classes around it, so most of its variance is not
explained by anything this program can name.

Its clearest jobs are a few specific spots, which this program predicts:
- the blank line ("\n\n") right after an opening "<think>" (about +3.3) or a closing
  "</think>" (about +2.5) in a chat-template turn. There it is strongly on, and its causal
  importance is near 1, so this is the part the model uses.
- the end-of-document token "<|endoftext|>" (about +0.7).
- a run of spaces or tabs continuing after another such token (about +0.3).

0 on the first token of each document, where the component is silent.

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Value of the blank line right after each chat think tag, from the training data.
AFTER_TAG = {"<think>": 3.3, "</think>": 2.5}
END_OF_DOCUMENT = 0.7  # the <|endoftext|> token
SPACE_RUN = 0.3  # a spaces-or-tabs token after another one
MEAN = -0.04  # the component's average activation, everywhere else


def is_spaces(s):
    """True for a token made only of spaces or tabs (no newline)."""
    return s != "" and s.strip(" \t") == ""


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    tokens = prefix.token_strings
    same_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) >= 2 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]

        return carry, AFTER_TAG[before]
    if now == "<|endoftext|>":
        return carry, END_OF_DOCUMENT
    if is_spaces(now) and is_spaces(before):
        return carry, SPACE_RUN
    return carry, MEAN

simple token, position or word-class structure that we could find: predicting
the activation from the current token's identity explains about 2% of its
variance on held-out text, and token class, position and previous token explain
less than 1%. So the best simple program is the component's typical value,
a constant near its mean of -0.01.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = -0.01


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    return carry, MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Reads mainly MLP hidden unit 4979 of layer 15: the component's input weight is dominated by
that unit, and the unit alone correlates about 0.73 with the component's activation.

What it responds to: reports of how a command or test run ended. The strongest responses are on
"finished", "completed" and "ran", and they are much larger inside tool output (the text between
<tool_response> and the end of that turn), as in "[Command finished with exit code 0]" and
"[The command completed with exit code 0]". Inside tool output "command" and "with" also respond,
and other outcome words ("passed", "successfully", "failed", "result", "tests" ...) respond
weakly. Every other token is predicted as 0, apart from a small value for tool-output text.
The rest of the component's variance is spread thinly over ordinary text (spaces, commas, "the",
digits) with no token or context concept that explains it, so this program explains only a small
share of the activation.
"""

READS = ()

# Words that say a process or test run went through, and how it ended.
STRONG = frozenset("finished completed ran".split())
COMMAND = frozenset("command with".split())
OUTCOME = frozenset(
    """exit code successfully success successful passed failed failure result results tests test
    running did""".split()
)
TOOL_OPEN = "<tool_response>"
TOOL_CLOSE = ("</tool_response>", "<|im_end|>")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (recent text, inside a tool response, document id of the last token)
    buf, in_tool, doc = carry if carry is not None else ("", False, None)
    if prefix.document_ids[-1] != doc:  # a new document: the state starts afresh
        buf, in_tool = "", False
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    buf = (buf + tok)[-60:]
    opened = buf.rfind(TOOL_OPEN)
    closed = max(buf.rfind(c) for c in TOOL_CLOSE)
    if opened > closed:
        in_tool = True
    elif closed > opened:
        in_tool = False
    word = tok.strip().lower()
    if word in STRONG:
        value = 12.0 if in_tool else 4.0
    elif word in COMMAND and in_tool:
        value = 6.0
    elif word in OUTCOME:
        value = 2.0 if in_tool else 0.4
    else:
        value = 0.25 if in_tool else 0.0
    return (buf, in_tool, prefix.document_ids[-1]), value

"""Layer 15, MLP hidden unit 4980 (the down_proj component 4980), as a word detector.

What it responds to: the word where a single point, item or quantity is being set up, as in
"only one thing", "one goal", "two reasons", "one thing is clear:", "is simple", "the same",
"the following". Its output promotes ":" and "—" (logit lens), so it marks the spot where the
text is about to name the one point at issue.

This program scores each word from its own word class (counting words, point nouns, framing
words), and gives a larger value to a few phrases where the word completes a set-up phrase
("one thing", "one question", "is simple", "only one"). It reads only the current and previous
word, so it is causal. Values are in the component's own activation units.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Counting words: "one", "two", "only one", "a single".
COUNT = {"one": 1.2, "two": 1.5, "three": 0.9, "only": 1.2, "single": 0.6}
# Nouns for the one point at issue: "one thing", "one goal", "the question".
POINT = {"thing": 0.6, "things": 0.6, "goal": 2.0, "question": 1.2, "idea": 1.5,
         "reason": 0.8, "aim": 0.8, "point": 0.8, "suggestion": 0.8, "remark": 0.8,
         "factor": 0.8, "option": 0.8, "advantage": 0.8, "problem": 0.8, "answer": 0.8,
         "secret": 0.8}
# Words that frame a single point: "is simple", "is clear", "the same", "the following".
FRAME = {"simple": 2.2, "clear": 1.6, "same": 1.0, "sure": 1.0, "certain": 1.0,
         "following": 1.7, "another": 1.0, "something": 1.1, "main": 0.8, "basic": 0.8,
         "common": 0.8, "key": 0.8}
# Set-up phrases: the mean activation on the second word, measured on training text.
PHRASE = {("one", "thing"): 13.0, ("one", "question"): 11.0, ("two", "things"): 9.0,
          ("is", "simple"): 9.0, ("very", "simple"): 6.0, ("only", "one"): 4.5,
          ("only", "thing"): 5.5, ("have", "one"): 5.0, ("but", "one"): 5.5,
          ("the", "only"): 3.3, ("are", "two"): 3.3, ("thing", "is"): 5.0,
          ("the", "following"): 2.5}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    value = COUNT.get(cur, 0.0) + POINT.get(cur, 0.0) + FRAME.get(cur, 0.0)
    if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower()
        if (prev, cur) in PHRASE:
            value = max(value, PHRASE[(prev, cur)])
    return carry, float(value)

"""Token-category predictor for the component's activation.

Weak signal only: the component's activation is mostly context-dependent noise,
and only a few token classes shift its average.
- Chat / special markers (<|im_start|>, <tool_call>, ...) and modal verbs
  (can, may, could, would, ...) sit slightly above average.
- The word "or" (and "nor") sits clearly below average.
Everything else gets the overall mean, about 0.047.
"""

import re

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

MEAN = 0.047
MARKER_OR_MODAL = 0.13
OR_WORDS = -0.17
MODALS = {"can", "may", "could", "would", "should", "will", "might", "must"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    if text.lower() in ("or", "nor"):
        return None, OR_WORDS
    if re.fullmatch(r"<[^>]*>", text) or text.lower() in MODALS:
        return None, MARKER_OR_MODAL
    return None, MEAN

"""Restriction and condition wording, read off the text so far.

Hidden unit 4982 of layer 15's MLP (the component's input direction is almost all
this one unit) writes toward words like "constraints", "restrictions", "conditions"
and "requirements". It is strongly positive on the words that set up a condition or a
limit, most of all "to" or "that" right after "subject", "provided" or "compliance"
("subject to", "provided that", "compliance with"), and mildly positive on the limit
and obligation words themselves. Most other tokens sit near zero, and this program
predicts zero there. A small negative value on "will" and on section headers like
"References" follows the weak negative side.
"""
READS = ()

SETUP = {"subject", "provided", "compliance", "open", "agree", "condition", "conditions"}
LIMIT_WORDS = {
    "subject", "provided", "compliance", "except", "unless", "without", "limit", "limits",
    "limited", "limitation", "limitations", "restriction", "restrictions", "restricted",
    "condition", "conditions", "requirement", "requirements", "minimum", "maximum",
    "exception", "permitted", "eligible", "applicable", "must", "cannot", "may",
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower() if prefix.position > 0 else ""
    if cur in ("to", "that", "with") and prev in SETUP:
        return carry, 3.0
    if cur in LIMIT_WORDS:
        return carry, 0.7
    if cur == "will":
        return carry, -0.3
    if cur == "references":
        return carry, -1.0
    return carry, 0.0

"""Layer 15, MLP hidden unit 4983: the "abstract noun ... of" unit.

The unit's activation is almost exactly this one hidden unit of the layer-15 MLP.
It goes strongly negative on the head noun of a formal "the <abstract noun> of ..."
phrase, such as "the presence of", "the existence of", "the use of", "the development
of", and on the "of" (or its foreign equivalent: de, des, der, ...) that follows such a
noun. The more abstract the noun, the more negative. The same nouns with no determiner
before them ("your online presence") are only mildly negative. Everything else is near 0.

Values (in activation units, typical of the strong cases):
  listed abstract noun after the/this/its/...   -5.2
  listed abstract noun with no determiner       -1.2
  noun ending in an abstract suffix, after one  -1.3   (otherwise -0.6)
  "of" right after a listed abstract noun       -4.5
  "of" right after a suffix noun                -2.7
  any other "of" (or de/des/der/...)            -0.5
  everything else                                0

Left out: the unit's small, diffuse positive background on ordinary words (the, comma,
period, to, and), and the long tail of other formal nouns that are not on the list.
"""

READS = ()

# Nouns for states, qualities, processes and events that usually take an "of" complement.
ABSTRACT_NOUNS = frozenset("""
presence existence absence availability use development formation nature importance lack
effectiveness efficiency accuracy success performance quality safety stability status
strength ability capacity application implementation creation production generation
introduction inclusion removal expansion increase decrease reduction growth rise spread
occurrence prevalence frequency significance validity viability integrity appearance
execution operation management treatment preparation evolution discovery identification
determination estimation calculation improvement impact effect role extent amount level
degree length beauty health design function process release addition detection difficulty
need possibility quantity magnitude variation regulation adoption assignment induction
activation dependence necessity relevance rarity ease intensity complexity diversity
elimination maintenance construction establishment deployment delivery exposure
value fact size structure location scope provision direction potential expression change
influence cost movement relationship failure loss origin usefulness emergence completion
combination definition shape meaning distribution effects behavior truth sale choice arrival
correctness severity likelihood enactment filing selection synthesis thickness rotation
activity opening return outcome appointment relation speed security content death
""".split())

# Nouns ending in suffixes that make abstract nouns (existence, validity, darkness, ...).
ABSTRACT_SUFFIXES = ("ence", "ance", "ency", "ancy", "ity", "ness", "ment", "tion", "sion")

DETERMINERS = frozenset(
    "the this that its their his her our any each such these those a an".split()
)

# "of" and its equivalents in other languages.
OF_WORDS = frozenset(["of", "de", "des", "der", "von", "van", "di", "del", "della"])


def noun_value(word, after_determiner):
    """The activation a completed word gives when it is a noun of this kind."""
    if word in ABSTRACT_NOUNS:
        return -5.2 if after_determiner else -1.2
    if word.endswith(ABSTRACT_SUFFIXES) and len(word) > 5:
        return -1.3 if after_determiner else -0.6
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry["doc"] != doc:
        carry = {"doc": doc, "word": "", "last_word": "", "prev": ""}
    text = token.strip().lower()
    letters = text.isalpha()
    # A letter token with no leading space continues the word being built (e.g. "ness").
    if letters and not token.startswith(" ") and carry["word"]:
        word = carry["word"] + text
    else:
        word = text if letters else ""
    if text in OF_WORDS:
        last = carry["last_word"]
        if last in ABSTRACT_NOUNS:
            value = -4.5
        elif last.endswith(ABSTRACT_SUFFIXES) and len(last) > 5:
            value = -2.7
        else:
            value = -0.5
    else:
        value = noun_value(word, carry["prev"] in DETERMINERS)
    new = {"doc": doc, "word": word, "last_word": word, "prev": text}
    return new, float(value)

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 4984: a "group of people" detector.

The component is mostly quiet, and when it fires it is strongly negative. It fires on
words that name a group of people, and most strongly on groups of skilled people or
staff in a business or expertise setting: "our team of experts", "a team of experienced
chemists", "his people", "the staff", "engineers", "researchers", "crew", "troops".
Ordinary group words ("members", "community", "government", "students") are weaker,
and a sports team is near zero.

Predicted activation, per word, in four steps:
  1. a group noun (a list of nouns for people and groups, a short list of such nouns in
     other languages, plus agentive nouns such as "reform|ers" and "Marx|ists", checked
     against WordNet) takes a base value: about -4.7
     for a specialist group (experts, staff, crew, troops, ...) and about -1.5 for other
     groups;
  2. a possessive or quantifier right before it ("our", "his", "some", "many") makes it
     about 1.6 times stronger;
  3. a company or expertise word among the six words before it ("our", "we", "company",
     "experienced", "skilled", ...) makes it about 1.7 times stronger;
  4. weaker negatives for words that stand for people: "who", "those", "others" (about
     -1.3), "we", "they", "some", "many", "everyone" (about -0.6); "of" right after a group
     noun ("members of", "team of", about -0.9); "by" and "et" (about -0.5).

The program tracks the current whole word (letters of the current token plus any letters
of earlier tokens that continue it) and a short memory of the words before it, reset at
each document boundary. Its values are hand-set from the activation averages; they are
not fitted to the activations beyond that.
"""

READS = ()

# Nouns for groups or categories of people, a hand-made concept list.
GROUP_NOUNS = frozenset(
    """people person team teams staff crew members member group groups experts expert
    officials official troops soldiers colleagues colleague friends friend folks guys
    supporters researchers scientists engineers developers leaders doctors workers worker
    employees employee volunteers officers police students men women citizens residents
    families family committee board majority crowd personnel faculty delegation government
    community army militia rebels fans followers voters activists enthusiasts professionals
    individuals kids children boys girls youths elders priests monks scholars critics
    teachers nurses lawyers judges warriors fighters pioneers settlers founders executives
    directors managers representatives delegates technicians designers analysts authors
    writers artists players parents neighbors tribe tribes clan party parties council
    congress senate panel unit squad force forces""".split()
)

# The specialist groups: professionals, experts, staff, military and active crowds.
SPECIALIST_GROUPS = frozenset(
    """experts expert engineers scientists researchers developers designers professionals
    technicians doctors nurses scholars analysts consultants specialists executives authors
    writers lawyers judges teachers coaches planners academics historians soldiers troops
    officers militia crew supporters activists enthusiasts volunteers fans guys folks
    colleagues staff committee""".split()
)

# Group nouns in other languages (team, staff, specialists, people, friend, member).
OTHER_LANGUAGE_GROUPS = frozenset(
    """equipe équipe equipo equipa quipe chercheurs hommes gens personas gente pessoas
    esperti patriotas mitglieder freunde leute люди ученые команда 团队 队 人 专家 朋友
    成员 同事 员 者 们""".split()
)

# Words that open a noun phrase about a person or group: possessives and quantifiers.
POSSESSIVE_OR_QUANTIFIER = frozenset(
    """our his my your their its her whose some many few several these those all most
    both""".split()
)

# Words that mark a company or expertise setting, which strengthens a group noun after them.
COMPANY_OR_EXPERTISE = frozenset(
    """our we company services clients customers solutions quality industry experience
    experienced professional professionals dedicated qualified skilled expert experts
    highly""".split()
)

# Pronouns and quantifiers that can stand for people.
PEOPLE_PRONOUNS = frozenset(
    "we they us them others those everyone someone anyone many some who whom".split()
)

# Words after which "of" introduces the people in a group ("members of", "team of").
GROUP_OF_WORDS = GROUP_NOUNS | frozenset("part one member rest bunch band host number".split())

# Suffixes of agentive nouns; a word with one counts as a person noun if WordNet says so.
AGENT_SUFFIXES = ("ists", "ians", "ers", "ors", "ants", "ents")

WINDOW = 6  # how many earlier words the context check looks back over


def _is_person_noun(word):
    import wordnet

    cats = set()
    for base in [word] + list(wordnet.base_forms(word)):
        cats |= set(c for c in wordnet.categories(base) if c.startswith("noun."))
    return "noun.person" in cats or "noun.group" in cats


def _track(carry, prefix):
    """The last WINDOW earlier whole words and the current word, after the newest token."""
    done, cur = carry if carry is not None else ((), "")
    if len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        done, cur = (), ""  # a new document starts: forget the words before it
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    core = tok.strip().lower()
    if core.isalpha() and not tok.startswith(" "):
        cur = cur + core  # the token continues the current word
    elif core.isalpha():
        done, cur = _push(done, cur), core  # a new word starts here
    else:
        done, cur = _push(done, cur), ""  # punctuation or space ends the word
    return done, cur


def _push(done, cur):
    return (done + (cur,))[-WINDOW:] if cur else done


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    done, cur = _track(carry, prefix)
    prev = done[-1] if done else ""
    is_group = (
        cur in GROUP_NOUNS
        or cur in OTHER_LANGUAGE_GROUPS
        or (cur.endswith(AGENT_SUFFIXES) and len(cur) > 4 and _is_person_noun(cur))
    )
    if is_group:
        value = -4.7 if cur in SPECIALIST_GROUPS else -1.5
        if prev in POSSESSIVE_OR_QUANTIFIER:
            value *= 1.6
        if any(w in COMPANY_OR_EXPERTISE for w in done):
            value *= 1.7
    elif cur in {"who", "those", "others"}:
        value = -1.3
    elif cur in PEOPLE_PRONOUNS:
        value = -0.6
    elif cur == "of" and prev in GROUP_OF_WORDS:
        value = -0.9
    elif cur in {"by", "et"}:
        value = -0.5
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return (done, cur), value

The component mostly reads MLP hidden unit 4988 of layer 15 (about 63% of its input
weight). Its activation is large in both directions, but spread over very common tokens
(commas, periods, digits, "the", "is") and driven by context.

What this program does: it predicts the word-level tendencies that are clearest in the
data. Words that announce an event, a notice or an attention-getting moment ("suddenly",

    "unfortunate", "glad", "okay", "why", "lucky", "very",
}

"""A weak, mostly-flat predictor of one component (layer 15 MLP down_proj, unit 4989).

What the component does: its activation is diffuse, centred slightly above zero (mean 0.06),
and it is silent (about 0) on the first token of each document. Its large negative values
sit on academic field names used as a field, e.g. "in [mathematics]", "the fun of [physics]",
"[statistics] and", "[calculus] of"; there it can reach -5 to -10. But the same words are
often positive or near zero in other contexts, so no token rule explains most of it.

This program: 0 at each document's first token; a small negative value (-0.3) on a
WordNet academic-discipline word right after a framing word ("in", "of", "field",
"world", "fun", "study", "branch", "applied", "theory", "and"); the typical level 0.056
everywhere else.
"""
from functools import lru_cache

import wordnet

READS = ()
TYPICAL = 0.056
FIELD_FRAME = {"in", "of", "field", "world", "fun", "study", "branch", "applied", "theory", "and"}


@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def is_discipline(token):
    word = token.strip().lower()
    return word.isalpha() and wordnet.is_a(word, "discipline")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    if t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[t] != prefix.document_ids[t - 1]:
        return carry, 0.0
    word = prefix.token_strings[t]
    before = prefix.token_strings[t - 1].strip().lower()
    if before in FIELD_FRAME and is_discipline(word):
        return carry, -0.3
    return carry, TYPICAL
